The '''Owari clan''' is a [[Japanese clans|Japanese clan]]. The clan were originally [[Kuni no miyatsuko]] but after the abolition of the role they took on a priestly role at [[:en:Atsuta Jingu|Atsuta Jingu]]. They share this history with the [[Izumo clan]] of [[Izumo-taisha]], the [[Aso clan]] of [[Aso Shrine]], the {{ill|Munakata clan|ja|宗像氏|fr|Clan Munakata}} of [[Munakata Taisha]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Matsunaga |first=Naomichi |title=Kuni no miyatsuko |url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=8839 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20231025020641/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=8839 |archive-date=2023-10-25 |access-date=2023-10-25 |website=Kokugakuin University Encyclopedia of Shinto |language=en}}</ref> the [[Amabe clan]] of [[Kono Shrine]]<ref name="Bunka1">{{cite web |title=海部氏系図 |trans-title=Amebe shikeizu |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/201/777 |accessdate=August 20, 2020 |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |language=Japanese}}</ref> and the [[Yamato no Kuni no Miyatsuko|Yamato clan]] of [[Ōyamato Shrine]].

== History ==

=== Origins and genealogy ===
In ''{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|qid=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}}'', the descendants of [[Amatsuhikone]], [[Ame no Hohi]], and {{ill|Amanomichine|ja|天道根命}}, together with the descendants of Amenohoakari are referred to as ''Tenson-zoku''. The ''Tenson-zoku'' descended from [[Takamagahara]] (Plain of High {{ill|Heaven|en|Heaven|qid=Q4489450|lt=Heaven}}) to {{ill|Owari Province|en|Owari Province|qid=Q514506|lt=Owari}} and {{ill|Tanba Province|cs|Tanba (provincie)|de|Provinz Tamba|es|Provincia de Tanba|fa|ولایت تانبا|fr|Province de Tanba|gl|Provincia de Tanba|id|Provinsi Tamba|it|Tanba (provincia)|ja|丹波国|ko|단바국|lt|Tambos žemė|nl|Tamba (provincie)|pt|Província de Tanba|ru|Тамба (провинция)|simple|Tamba Province|sk|Tanba (provincia)|sr|Провинција Тамба|tr|Tamba (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Тамба|zh|丹波國|zh_min_nan|Tanba-kok|qid=Q954511|lt=Tanba}} provinces, and are considered to be the ancestors of the Owari clan, as well as three other clans {{ill|Tsumori clan|ja|津守氏|lt=Tsumori}}, [[Amabe clan|Amabe]], and {{ill|Tanba clan|ja|丹波氏|lt=Tanba}} clans.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Hanawa |first=Hokiichi |url=http://worldcat.org/oclc/959773242 |title=Shinsen Shōjiroku (新撰姓氏錄) |date=1983 |publisher=Onkogakkai |location=Japan |oclc=959773242}}</ref>

However, Toshio Hoga argues that ''{{nihongo|'''Amabe clan genealogy'''|海部氏系図|Amabe-shi Keizu|}},'' which records these four clans as descendants of Amenohoakari, is a forged document,<ref>{{Cite book |last=Hoga |first=Toshio |title=Kokuho「Amabe-shi Keizu」he no gimon, Kokigi no Heya (国宝「海部氏系図」への疑問 古樹紀之房間) |year=2006 |location=Japan}}</ref> and that these clans actually descended from the {{ill|List of water deities|en|List of water deities|qid=Q13416336|lt=sea deity}} {{ill|Watatsumi|abstract|Q1474187|az|Vatatsumi|de|Watatsumi|es|Watatsumi|fa|واتاتسومی|fr|Watatsumi|hu|Vatacumi|ja|ワタツミ|ko|와타쓰미|mni|ꯋꯇꯠꯁꯨꯃꯤ|pl|Watatsumi|ru|Ватацуми|simple|Watatsumi|uk|Вататсумі|zh|綿津見|qid=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi}}. In addition, Owari clan's genealogy includes the great-grandson of Watatsumi, [[Takakuraji]], as their ancestor, and he argues this is the original genealogy.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Hoga |first=Toshio |title=Tango no Amabe-shi no Shutsuji to sono ichizoku, Kokigi no Heya (丹後の海部氏の出自とその一族) |year=2006 |location=Japan}}</ref>

=== Atsuta Shrine ===
The "Daijingu engi" records show that during Emperor Temmu's time, the divine sword [[Kusanagi no Tsurugi]] was returned to the palace. Seven guardians were then appointed to oversee its worship. These guardians were linked to [[Miyazu-hime]] and {{ill|Takeinadane|ja|建稲種命}}.<ref name="Ponsonby-Fane-2016" />

[[Miyazu-hime]] the wife of {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}} was a member of the clan<ref name="Ponsonby-Fane-2016">{{Cite book |last=Ponsonby-Fane |first=R. A. B. |title=Studies In Shinto & Shrines |date=2016-05-11 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-138-98322-9 |edition=1st |language=English |chapter=Atsuta Jingu}}</ref>

According to traditional sources, {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}} died in the 43rd year of Emperor Keiko's reign (景行天皇43rd year , equivalent 113 AD).<ref name="Ponsonby-Fane-2016" />{{rp|433}}  The possessions of the dead prince were gathered together along with the sword [[Kusanagi no Tsurugi|Kusanagi]]; and his widow [[Miyazu-hime]] venerated his memory in a shrine at her home. Sometime later, these relics and the sacred sword were moved to the current location of the Atsuta Shrine.<ref name="Ponsonby-Fane-2016" />{{rp|434}}

''Nihonshoki'' explains that this move occurred in the 51st year of Keiko's reign, but shrine tradition also dates this event in the 1st year of Emperor Chūai's reign.<ref name="Ponsonby-Fane-2016" />{{rp|435}}
The Owari clan established the [[:en:Atsuta Jingu|Atsuta Jingu]] in 192, and held the position of the shrine's high priest since ancient times, passing it down from generation to generation.<ref name="Naito-1975">{{Cite book |last=Naito |first=Toho |title=Choshu Zasshi (張州雑志) |publisher=Aichi-ken Kyōdo Shiryō Kankō-kai |year=1975 |doi=10.11501/9537297}}</ref> {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}} and [[Miyazu-hime]] and her brother {{ill|Takeinadane|ja|建稲種命}} are worshipped at the shrine.<ref name="Ponsonby-Fane-2016" />{{rp|429}}

When Miyazu-hime died, a shrine was set up in her honor in Hikami. Her clan members became priests there. Inatane, the eleventh descendant of Amenohoakari, founded the Owari clan. As a result, Atsuta Myojin became the Owari clan's Ujigami.<ref name="Ponsonby-Fane-2016" />

The shrine, originally a Betsugu, later became a Sessha. It was founded in the fourth year of Chtiai (195), about 80 years after Yamato Takeru no Mikoto's death. Miyazu-hime was young when she knew Yamato Takeru no Mikoto.<ref name="Ponsonby-Fane-2016" />

=== Later history ===
The "Owariuji keizu" and shrine records reveal that during the times of Emperors Temmu, Jito, and Mommu, Owari no Muraji Inaki and his son, Owari no Muraji Inaoki, were Daiguji. Tadashika held this office for 40 years, from 1045 to 1084. His grandson, Suenori, succeeded him.<ref name="Ponsonby-Fane-2016" />

Tadanobu's eldest son, Tadayori, was the first Horishi, later called Gonguji. Other positions included Sokengyo and Ouchibito. The Tajima Daiki, and Baba families were known as the Shinkwan.<ref name="Ponsonby-Fane-2016" />

Below the Shinkwan were the Negi, also called Churo. Notable families included Awata Mabito, Ohara Mabito, Hayashi Asomi, Matsuoka Mabito, and Kume. Some had rights to worship at Hikami Jinja.<ref name="Ponsonby-Fane-2016" />In 1114, Kazumoto handed the position over to {{ill|Fujiwara no Suenori|en|Fujiwara no Suenori|qid=Q11623142|lt=Fujiwara no Suenori}}, who was from the [[Fujiwara clan]].<ref name="Naito-1975" /> Since then, the Fujiwara clan became the head of Atsuta Shrine, while the Owari clan stepped down to the position of adjutant chief priest (''gongūji'').<ref name="Ota-1942">{{Cite book |last=Ota |first=Akira |title=Seishi Kakei Daijiten (姓氏家系大辞典) |publisher=Kokuminsha |year=1942 |volume=1 |pages=1038–1051 |oclc=21114789}}</ref>

In Hoei I (1704), the Daiguji's decision to appoint an Atsuta Hoshi from Jingu-ji led to protests from the Negi families. The protest was not successful.<ref name="Ponsonby-Fane-2016" />

== Lineage and descendant houses ==
The '''Owari clan''' (Owari-uji) is a clan that takes "Owari" as its family name.

According to the ''[[Nihon Shoki]]'', the clan traces its ancestral deity to [[Ame-no-Hoakari]] and is said to have begun with [[Ame no Oshihito]]<ref>{{Cite book|和書|title=日本書紀|pages=巻第二の一書（第六第八）}}</ref>.

After residing in [[Mino Province|Mino]] and [[Hida Province|Hida]], the clan became the [[Owari-no-kuni-no-miyatsuko]] during the time of [[Ototoyomimi]]. During the era of [[Yamato Takeru]], they moved their base south of [[Atsuta Shrine|Atsuta]]. [[Miyazu-hime]] became a consort of Yamato Takeru, and the [[Kusanagi|Kusanagi sacred sword]] was enshrined at Atsuta. The main lineage of the Owari Sukune descendants served successive generations as [[Daiguji|Grand Shrine Masters]] of [[Atsuta Shrine]].

Descendants of the Owari [[Sukune]] include the Moriobe Sukune of Atsuta Shrine's Dainai family, [[Gon-guji]], and shrine priests of [[Hakkenjingu]]; the [[Baba clan]] of the chief inspector family; and the [[Tajima clan]] of the high priest family<ref>{{Cite book|和書|title=姓氏家系大辞典|year=1942|publisher=国民社|pages=尾張條、守部條、大喜條}}</ref>. Related clans include the [[Tsumori clan]], a shrine family of [[Sumiyoshi Taisha]] in [[Sumiyoshi-ku, Osaka|Sumiyoshi Ward]], [[Osaka]]; and the [[Amabe clan]], a shrine family of [[Kono Shrine]] in [[Miyazu, Kyoto]] (according to the National Treasure ''[[Amabe clan genealogy]]'').

Also recorded in the clan infobox of the Japanese article merged here: the clan titles 尾張連 and later 尾張宿禰; the classification 神別 (天孫); a base in Aichi District, Owari Province (尾張国愛知郡); the progenitor 天忍人命; the members 尾張大隅, 尾張草香, 尾張馬身, 尾張兼時 and 尾張浜主; and the descendant houses 熱田神宮家, 海部氏, 津守氏 and 村国氏.

== Cultural influence ==
According to one theory [[Danpusan Kofun]] is the tomb of a powerful chieftain of the Owari clan, perhaps {{ill|Owari no Kusaka|ja|尾張草香|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Owari no Kusaka|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11465318}}, who is mentioned in the ''[[Kojiki]]'' and ''[[Nihon Shoki]]'' chronicles of the {{ill|Nara period|en|Nara period|qid=Q189178|lt=Nara period}}, and whose daughter married the semi-legendary {{ill|Emperor Keitai|en|Emperor Keitai|qid=Q349277|lt=Emperor Keitai}} and who was the mother of [[Emperor Ankan]] and {{ill|Emperor Senka|en|Emperor Senka|qid=Q329728|lt=Emperor Senka}}.<ref name="Shiseki">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref> According to legend [[Miyazu-hime]] a member of the clan is buried in [[Danpusan Kofun]].<ref name="Shiseki2">{{cite book |last1=Isomura |first1=Yukio |title=(国指定史跡事典) National Historic Site Encyclopedia |last2=Sakai |first2=Hideya |date=2012 |publisher=学生社 |isbn=978-4311750403}}{{in lang|ja}}</ref>

The Owari clan was influential on the development of the [[Kujiki]].<ref name="Aoki-1998" /> It was mainly written as a compilation of elements from the [[Kojiki]], [[Nihon Shoki|Nihongi]] and [[Kogo Shūi|Kogo Shui]], likely by an author from the [[Mononobe clan]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Maxey |first=Trent E. |date=February 2013 |title=John Breen and Mark Teeuwen: A New History of Shinto. (Blackwell Brief Histories of Religion Series.) viii, 264 pp. Chichester: Wiley-Blackwell, 2010. ISBN 978 1 4051 5515 1. |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1017/s0041977x12001796 |journal=Bulletin of the School of Oriental and African Studies |volume=76 |issue=1 |pages=176–177 |doi=10.1017/s0041977x12001796 |s2cid=178230959 |issn=0041-977X}}</ref>{{rp|31}} However it also contains unique elements from neither. Book 5 is believed to preserve traditions of the [[Mononobe clan|Mononobe]] and Owari clans not found elsewhere, and Book 10 preserves the earlier historical record the {{Nihongo|Record of the Provincial governors|国造本紀|Kokuzō Hongi}}.<ref name="Aoki-1998">{{cite encyclopedia |year=1998 |title=Sendai Kuji Hongi |encyclopedia=Sekai Dai-Hyakkajiten |publisher=Heibonsha |url=http://kotobank.jp/word/%E5%85%88%E4%BB%A3%E6%97%A7%E4%BA%8B%E6%9C%AC%E7%B4%80 |access-date=July 22, 2013 |last=Aoki |first=Kazuo |author-link=Kazuo Aoki |editor1-last=Katō |editor1-first=Shūichi |editor1-link=Shūichi Katō (critic)}}</ref>

The Owari clan established the [[:en:Atsuta Jingu|Atsuta Jingu]].<ref name="Ota-1942"/>[[File:Yoritomo ubuyu.jpg|thumb|227x227px|Monument of [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]]'s birthplace, Suenori's villa, at {{ill|Seigan-ji (Atsuta-ku, Nagoya)|en|Seigan-ji (Atsuta-ku, Nagoya)|qid=Q17220718|lt=Seigan-ji}}.]]

== The Owari clan from the perspective of the Kinai regime ==
In the ''[[Nihon Shoki]]'', they are considered descendants of [[Ame-no-Hoakari]], and from early in the imperial genealogy, the Owari clan was connected to the emperors, frequently providing consorts. The distant ancestor [[Okitsu Yoso]]'s sister, [[Yosotahonomihime]] (Sesoku-hime), became the [[Empress]] of the 5th Emperor [[Kōshō]], and her son became the 6th Emperor [[Kōan]]. The 10th Emperor [[Sujin]] took [[Owari Ōamihime]] as his consort.

[[Takeina-dane-no-Mikoto]], son of [[Owari-no-kuni-no-miyatsuko]] [[Ototoyomimi]], accompanied [[Yamato Takeru]] (Ousu, the prince of the 12th Emperor [[Keikō]]) on his eastern expedition as vice-general and achieved military merit. His sister [[Miyazu-hime]] (Miyazuhime in the ''Nihon Shoki'', Miyazuhime in the ''Kojiki'') was wed in Owari on the return journey from the eastern expedition, and she enshrined the [[Kusanagi]] sword that had been entrusted to her and built [[Atsuta Shrine]]. Takeina-dane's son [[Otsunanemikoto]] served as [[Ōomi|Minister]] during the reign of Emperor Ōjin, and his son [[Owari no Ōhoko]] became Minister during the reign of Emperor Nintoku. The 15th Emperor [[Ōjin]] took [[Nakatsuhime]], granddaughter of Takeina-dane, as his empress.

The principal consort of the 26th Emperor [[Keitai]] before he entered Yamato Province was Mekohime, daughter of [[Owari no Muraji Kusaka]]. His first son, Prince Magari no Ōe, ascended as the 27th Emperor [[Ankan]], and his second son, Prince Hinokuma no Takata, ascended as the 28th Emperor [[Senka]]. Emperor Senka's daughter, [[Princess Ishihime]], became the empress of the 29th Emperor Kinmei and gave birth to the 30th Emperor [[Bidatsu]]. Emperor Bidatsu and [[Empress]] Nukatabe (the 33rd Emperor [[Suiko]]) had a son named [[Prince Owari]].

During the [[Jinshin War]], the clan fully supported [[Emperor Tenmu|Prince Ōama]], who had been raised by the Amabe clan, providing their private residence and funds, and made outstanding contributions to his ascension as the 40th Emperor [[Tenmu]]. In the 5th month of the 10th year of Empress Jitō ([[696]]), there is a record of [[Owari no Sukune Ōsumi]] being granted [[court rank]] and merit fields. According to the 12th month entry of the 1st year of Tenpyō-hōji ([[757]]) in the ''Shoku Nihongi'', this sudden bestowal of rewards was due to meritorious service in the [[Jinshin War]]{{要出典|date=2022年3月}}.

A clan bearing the Owari surname also existed in [[Inaba Province]]. This Owari clan was a powerful family that served as district magistrate of [[Yagami District, Tottori|Yagami]], and by the end of the [[Heian period]], members of the clan including the [[Saji clan]] and [[Hikita clan]] grew as development lords. Among these, the Saji clan became [[gokenin]] of the [[Kamakura shogunate]], and [[Saji Shigesada]], who distinguished himself in the [[Wada Conflict]], is known to have been appointed as [[jitō|land steward]] of [[Saji-gō]]. Compared to the cadet branches, little is known in detail about the main line of the Owari clan.
